entrypoints.summary: Library formatting invokes the fmt::Pointer implementations for Atomic<T> and Shared<'_, T>.
The advisory identifies formatting of values created with Atomic::null or Shared::null as examples of affected behavior.

sources.concept: Formatting an Atomic or Shared value with an invalid underlying pointer

impact.affected_asset: Memory safety and availability of the process performing the formatting.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause an affected library caller to format an Atomic or Shared value whose underlying pointer is invalid; null constructors are documented examples.
impact.security_effect: Invalid pointer dereference during library formatting.

causal_trace.summary: An Atomic<T> or Shared<'_, T> has an invalid underlying pointer; the advisory gives null values created by Atomic::null or Shared::null as examples.
The pre-fix fmt::Pointer implementations decomposed the stored data and, for a non-null raw value, called unsafe T::as_ptr(raw).cast::<()>() before formatting.
Formatting dereferenced the underlying pointer through the prior pointer-conversion path even though formatting a pointer value must not require the underlying pointer to be valid.
An invalid-pointer dereference occurs during formatting of affected Atomic or Shared values.

failure.operation: Invalid dereference of the underlying pointer during fmt::Pointer formatting

primary_invariant.statement: fmt::Pointer for Atomic<T> and Shared<'_, T> must format the decomposed raw pointer without dereferencing or otherwise requiring validity of its pointee.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The prior non-null branch converted raw with unsafe T::as_ptr(raw).cast::<()>(), and the advisory states the affected formatting implementation dereferenced the underlying pointer.

quality.review_notes: The advisory and inspected immutable patch establish the affected versions, formatting mechanism, and fix. The bundle contains no issue-specific regression test, reproducer, sanitizer output, or observed execution result, so no harness/oracle is asserted. The threat boundary is library-caller controlled rather than a demonstrated remote boundary.

remediation.invariant_restored: The patched implementations pass raw directly to fmt::Pointer::fmt and no longer invoke T::as_ptr in these formatting paths.
mitigation_classes: avoid dereferencing pointee while formatting pointer value

target.component: fmt::Pointer implementations for Atomic<T> and Shared<'_, T> in crossbeam-epoch/src/atomic.rs
